```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var event = {
    title:       'WOMBAT 2026',
    description: 'Workshop Organised by the Monash Business Analytics Team. Learn and discuss open-source tools for business analytics and data science.',
    location:    'Melbourne, Australia',
    url:         'https://wombat.numbat.space',
    startDate:   '20261130',   // YYYYMMDD (all-day)
    endDate:     '20261202',   // iCal end is exclusive, so +1 day after last day
    startDateHuman: '2026-11-30',
    endDateHuman:   '2026-12-01'
  };

  var ics = [
    'BEGIN:VCALENDAR',
    'VERSION:2.0',
    'PRODID:-//WOMBAT 2026//EN',
    'CALSCALE:GREGORIAN',
    'METHOD:PUBLISH',
    'BEGIN:VEVENT',
    'UID:wombat-2026@numbat.space',
    'DTSTAMP:' + new Date().toISOString().replace(/[-:]/g, '').split('.')[0] + 'Z',
    'DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:' + event.startDate,
    'DTEND;VALUE=DATE:'   + event.endDate,
    'SUMMARY:'      + event.title,
    'DESCRIPTION:'  + event.description,
    'LOCATION:'     + event.location,
    'URL:'          + event.url,
    'END:VEVENT',
    'END:VCALENDAR'
  ].join('\r\n');

  var icsDataURI = 'data:text/calendar;charset=utf-8,' + encodeURIComponent(ics);

  var googleURL = 'https://calendar.google.com/calendar/render?action=TEMPLATE' +
    '&text='     + encodeURIComponent(event.title) +
    '&dates='    + event.startDate + '/' + event.endDate +
    '&details='  + encodeURIComponent(event.description) +
    '&location=' + encodeURIComponent(event.location) +
    '&sprop=website:' + encodeURIComponent(event.url);

  var outlookURL = 'https://outlook.live.com/calendar/0/deeplink/compose?path=/calendar/action/compose&rru=addevent' +
    '&subject='   + encodeURIComponent(event.title) +
    '&startdt='   + event.startDateHuman +
    '&enddt='     + event.endDateHuman +
    '&body='      + encodeURIComponent(event.description) +
    '&location='  + encodeURIComponent(event.location) +
    '&allday=true';

  document.getElementById('cal-google').href  = googleURL;
  document.getElementById('cal-outlook').href = outlookURL;
  document.getElementById('cal-ical').href    = icsDataURI;

  // The Register → Live Schedule swap itself is handled by the shared
  // body.event-live class from js/live-status.html (see css/hero.css),
  // so the event dates only need to live in one place.
})();
</script>
```

## Keynote

```{=html}

  <div class="keynote-card" id="keynote-card">
    
    <!-- Left/Top Column: Speaker Profile -->
    <div class="profile-section">
      <div class="avatar-wrapper">
        <img src="img/keynote.png" alt="Rob J Hyndman" class="avatar">
      </div>
      <div class="speaker-info">
        <h2 class="speaker-name" data-anchor-id="keynote">Rob J Hyndman</h2>
        <p class="speaker-role">
          <span class="highlight-title">Professor of Statistics</span><br>
          Department of Econometrics and Business Statistics<br>
          <span class="institution">Monash Business School</span>
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Right/Bottom Column: Topic, Abstract & Bio -->
    <div class="content-section">
      <div class="topic-header">
        <h3 class="topic-title">Spotting the weird ones</h3>
      </div>
      
      <!-- Abstract: Visible by Default -->
      <div class="abstract-section">
        <p>Data analysis is about finding the stories hidden in the mass of information that make up a data set. Usually we are interested in understanding the major patterns and the relationships that hold true for most of the data. But sometimes we need to look at the weird observations, the mavericks, the ones that don’t follow the crowd and behave differently. These observations are called <strong>‘anomalies’</strong>.</p>
        <p>I will describe a principled statistical approach to identifying anomalies in diverse data sets, from simple numerical data to complex high-dimensional data objects. The ideas will be illustrated using the <code class="code-badge">{weird}</code> package for R applied to several data analysis problems, including spotting over-priced wines, identifying errors in the records of the Old Faithful Geyser, and uncovering forgotten epidemics in 19th century France.</p>
      </div>

      <!-- Toggle Trigger for Bio -->
      <button class="expand-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="bio-details">
        <span class="toggle-text">Read bio</span>
        <svg class="chevron-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="18" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none"><path d="M6 9l6 6 6-6"/></svg>
      </button>

      <!-- Folded Content: Collapsible Bio -->
      <div class="folded-content" id="bio-details">
        <div class="inner-scroll">
          <div class="content-block">
            <h4>About Rob J Hyndman</h4>
            <p>Prof Hyndman holds the position of Vice-Chancellor’s Distinguished Professor of Statistics at Monash University, and is an internationally recognised expert in time series forecasting.</p>
            <p>He is a prolific writer, having authored more than 200 research papers and five books in statistical science, and has won awards for his research, teaching, consulting, and graduate supervision.</p>
            <p>His commitment to open research and teaching with open-source statistical software and online learning materials has had a major impact on the accessibility and practice of forecasting.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

</div>

<script>
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const card = document.getElementById("keynote-card");
  const toggleBtn = card.querySelector(".expand-toggle");
  const foldedContent = card.querySelector(".folded-content");
  const toggleText = card.querySelector(".toggle-text");

  toggleBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const isOpen = card.classList.toggle("is-expanded");
    foldedContent.classList.toggle("open");
    
    // Update accessibility attributes & text contextually
    toggleBtn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", isOpen);
    toggleText.textContent = isOpen ? "Hide Bio" : "Read more";
  });
});
</script>
```

```{=html}
  <script>
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const images = document.querySelectorAll(".gallery img");

  const observerOptions = {
    root: null, // uses the viewport
    rootMargin: "0px",
    threshold: 0.15 // Triggers when 15% of the image is visible
  };

  const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries, observer) => {
    entries.forEach(entry => {
      if (entry.isIntersecting) {
        // Scrolled IN view
        entry.target.classList.add("is-visible");
      } else {
        // Scrolled OUT of view
        entry.target.classList.remove("is-visible");
      }
    });
  }, observerOptions);

  images.forEach(img => observer.observe(img));
});
    </script>
```
